requirements.evidence: Most of the contract is implemented: data model (create_totems/totem_presets/totem_preset_queue migrations), pairing command with random_int + str_pad and 10-min expiry (TotemPairingCode.php:27-31), auth with lockForUpdate in a transaction plus the 400/401/200 shapes including entity (TotemAuthController.php:19-95), HS256 JWT with all claims, totem.auth middleware with intersection scope (TotemAuth.php:52-55), 404/403/422 ordering in the controllers, a 429 rate_limited renderer (bootstrap/app.php), CORS config and phpunit/env pins. Gaps: routes use `{entity}` with `Entity $entity` (routes/api.php:10-12) and no `:slug` binding is shown, so slug resolution depends on code outside the diff. An unknown entity slug produces a generic 404 model-not-found, not 403 forbidden. `IssueTicket` is not changed to validate against TotemPriorities, so the 'single source for issuance validation' requirement is only met at the controller. Queue `description`/`visual` are hard-coded (`'description' => null`, `'color' => '#0055FF'`). Format-failure (400) pairings are not audit-logged.

conventions.evidence: The change has no tests, which breaks the 'No production code without a test' rule. The controllers do not use `$request->validate`; manual checks are defensible here because of the custom error codes. New public methods have no PHPDoc. On the positive side, issuance reuses `App\Actions\IssueTicket` (TotemController.php:136), the models use `#[Fillable]`, the migrations have generated-style names and reversible down(), and CHANGELOG, docs/api/totem.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/database-schema.md are updated.

security.evidence: The JWT handling is sound: alg pinned to HS256, `hash_equals` signature check, exp checked, totem/preset active and entity cross-checks, scope intersected with the current join, the same 401 for every invalid code, the code never logged, the preset row locked. However, `$secret = (string) config('services.totem.jwt_secret')` (TotemAuthController.php:56, TotemAuth.php:23) silently becomes '' when TOTEM_JWT_SECRET is unset (.env.example ships it empty), so a misconfigured deployment signs and accepts tokens with an empty HMAC key that anyone can forge. Pairing-code collisions in the command are not handled.

tests.evidence: The diff adds no file under tests/. Pairing, JWT validation, middleware 401 cases, 403/404/422 paths, throttling, CORS and the artisan command are all untested, even though phpunit.xml was changed to pin a test secret.

simplicity.evidence: The entity-match check and the queue resolve/scope/active block are copy-pasted across priorities() and issueTicket() (TotemController.php:57-79 and 99-134). The middleware checks entity mismatch twice (TotemAuth.php:43-49), and the second check is redundant. TotemPriorities::find is called twice in issueTicket. Otherwise lean: a small HS256 helper and no service layer.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, but controller methods are long and repetitive. TotemAuthController::auth uses a thrown `\RuntimeException('invalid_pairing_code')` caught broadly as control flow, which would also mask unrelated RuntimeExceptions as 401. Some comments only restate the code (`// exp check`).

scope.evidence: The diff adds an empty `.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml` and a new `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, which are unrelated to the task (CHANGELOG already lists an existing CI test gate). Everything else serves the task.

issues.explanation: No Pest/PHPUnit tests ship with a new authentication flow, three endpoints, middleware and an artisan command, violating the mandatory test-first convention.
A missing TOTEM_JWT_SECRET is cast to an empty string and used as the HMAC key instead of failing, which makes tokens forgeable in a misconfigured environment.
`{entity}` is bound to `Entity $entity` without `:slug`, so slug lookup relies on unseen model configuration, and an unknown entity slug yields a generic 404 instead of 403 forbidden.
IssueTicket is not wired to TotemPriorities, so priority values are only enforced in the controller rather than through a single source used by issuance validation.
Queue `description` and `visual.color`/`icon` are hard-coded placeholders rather than queue data.
Invalid-format pairing attempts return 400 without an audit log entry, although the task asks to audit pairing failures.
Unrelated CI workflow files are added, one of them empty.
Entity check and queue resolve/scope/active logic are duplicated across endpoints.
A randomly generated code that collides with another preset's active code hits the unique index and throws instead of retrying; the factory has the same collision risk.
Using a generic RuntimeException for control flow and catching it broadly can mask unrelated errors as invalid_pairing_code.
The second entity-mismatch check is redundant after the first.

review.summary: The change implements the totem pairing flow, a hand-rolled HS256 JWT, the totem.auth middleware with intersection scoping, the three endpoints reusing IssueTicket, CORS, rate-limit rendering and doc updates, and most of the contract looks right. It ships no tests at all, which the project treats as mandatory, falls back to an empty JWT secret when unconfigured, depends on unseen slug binding for {entity}, and adds unrelated CI workflow files, so it needs substantial rework before merge.
